summary: The note describes Aurora's shift to community policing, launched through the "Neighborhood Guardians" program in September 2023 under Mayor Linda Harris and Police Chief Johnathan Brooks. It covers neighborhood kiosks, education workshops, technology tools (SafeStreets app, Predictive Patrol Mapping), body-worn cameras, and challenges such as mistrust, budget limits and internal skepticism. A February 2024 report links kiosks to reduced crime, and a comprehensive evaluation is planned for later in the year.
one_line: Aurora's Neighborhood Guardians program and related technology, kiosk and education efforts aim to build trust and reduce crime through community policing.
key_facts: The Aurora City Council, under Mayor Linda Harris, launched the "Neighborhood Guardians" community policing program on September 15, 2023.
Police Chief Johnathan Brooks said the aim is "to shift our focus from a solely responsive model to a proactive and inclusive approach."
As of October 1, 2023, ten neighborhood kiosks are operational for officers and residents to talk and work on safety initiatives.
The kiosk in Maplewood District hosts weekly meetings to develop strategies against recent upticks in petty crime.
Officer Maria Rodriguez hosts the "Law and Your Community" series at the Hamilton Community Center, saying "informed citizens are empowered citizens."
The "SafeStreets" mobile app launched on November 3, 2023, letting residents report non-emergency issues, view crime maps and receive real-time safety alerts.
The "Predictive Patrol Mapping" system, unveiled on December 8, 2023, analyzes crime patterns to help officers address potential trouble spots while respecting privacy and civil liberties.
Body-worn cameras have been deployed for all patrolling officers as of January 10, 2024, to support transparency and accountability.
Challenges include mistrust in marginalized communities, budget constraints, staffing limits, and skepticism among some officers accustomed to traditional policing.
Officer Kevin Jackson said "our resources are stretched thin."
The Aurora City Police Department's quarterly report released on February 15, 2024 showed reduced crime rates in neighborhoods where kiosks were implemented.
Shop owner Mark Thompson said he is now on a first-name basis with Officer Patel, who patrols his block.
A comprehensive evaluation of the initiatives is scheduled for later this year, and other cities are considering similar adaptations.
